transfer.summary: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. worldcup.title: ‘We are on the edge’: how Swedish league declined from summit of women’s game
worldcup.summary: The Damallsvenskan once mastered Europe and attracted the best players, but many are now worried for its future On 12 October 2003, Sweden stood still. The women’s football team were playing Germany in the World Cup final. TV4 set a new viewing record as almost half the nation watched the game go into extra time, where Nia Künzer scored the golden goal winner after 98 minutes. It was a bitter pill to swallow but there was still the belief that the tournament would mark the start of women’s football’s commercial breakthrough in Sweden. After all, how could sponsors and broadcasters ignore such undeniable interest? Continue reading...
